title: Kapangan snap bean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Kapangan snap bean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Kapangan snap bean is a pole snap bean variety. About 56 days to harvest, 13.6 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: Kapangan snap bean is a pole snap bean variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2008 as NSIC 2008 PSnBn 1. BSU IPB Highland Crops Research Station bred it. It takes about 56 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 13.59 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Kapangan snap bean takes about 56 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is about the average of the 8 pole snap bean varieties with a day count, 54.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 13.59 t/ha matches the average of its group, 14. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer).

The pests and diseases that hit snap bean fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its pods grew about 17.1 cm long. The seed coat is white.
Where and when to plant Kapangan snap bean

Baguio beans like cool weather, so most come from the highlands of Benguet and Mountain Province. Pole types bear longer, and bush types fit a short cropping gap. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 56 days from sowing to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 13.59 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Kapangan?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
